recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的細胞充滿粗大、深紫黑色的嗜鹼性顆粒，幾乎遮蔽細胞核，即為嗜鹼性球（basophil）；背景可見分葉中性球、帶狀核中性球與較大的骨髓細胞/前骨髓細胞，呈左移的顆粒球系，符合慢性骨髓性白血病（CML）的背景。
features: Arrowed cell about the size of a neutrophil, densely packed with coarse dark purple-black granules
Granules overlie and obscure the nucleus, so nuclear lobation is not discernible
Background shows segmented neutrophils, band forms and larger immature granulocytes (myelocyte/promyelocyte-like cells) indicating a left shift
A small lymphocyte and scattered platelets; red cells normocytic without significant poikilocytosis
No blasts clearly identified in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a basophil (arrow) with abundant coarse, dark purple-black cytoplasmic granules obscuring the nucleus. The background contains increased granulocytes at various stages of maturation, including segmented neutrophils, bands and immature myelocyte-like forms, reflecting a left-shifted granulocytic series. Red cells and platelets are unremarkable in this field and no blasts are seen. In the clinical context, basophilia with a left-shifted myeloid series is consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia.

ddx.vs: Mast cells are larger with a round central nucleus and more uniform, less overlapping metachromatic granules, and are CD117/tryptase positive.
Toxic granulation is finer and dispersed with a clearly visible segmented nucleus, not coarse granules obscuring the nucleus.
Eosinophils have refractile orange-red uniform granules and a visible bilobed nucleus rather than blue-black granules.
Precipitate is irregular and extends beyond the cell border, while basophil granules are confined to the cytoplasm.
